hypothesis: A fresh 15-minute price breakout aligned with 21/55-or-faster EMA direction and causal ten-level visible-book imbalance transfers to SP500 and SPCX with positive bidirectional after-cost validation performance when executed at the next bar's observed bid or ask.
decision: Reject this exact 192-configuration breakout-plus-visible-book-pressure family for SP500 and SPCX execution. The development-selected 32-bar, 21/55 EMA, absolute-imbalance 0.10, 120-bps-stop recipe lost on both assets in untouched validation under nominal friction and worsened under stress. Preserve the final chronological 20% holdout unopened. Do not add HIP-3 execution authority, increase leverage, or retune on validation to rescue the mechanism. Continue the distinct SNDK, GOLD, and BRENTOIL hypotheses after their archives pass exact audit; another entry/exit mechanism is a new pre-registered hypothesis.
falsifier: This exact-transfer rejection would be updated by a separately authorized one-time test of the frozen recipe on the sealed holdout or a fresh non-overlapping venue-matched window that is after-cost positive with aggregate profit factor above one, both directions represented, no single event dominating, and survival under the declared stress friction. A materially changed mechanism, source window, cost model, or selection protocol is new evidence rather than a falsification of this result.
limitations: L2 midpoint OHLC is a high-agreement price-path proxy, not public-trade OHLC; the completed archives contain no public trades.

Entries and scheduled exits use observed next-bar executable bid or ask, current modeled HIP-3 taker fees, authentic funding, and explicit latency, but do not reconstruct private queue position or adverse selection.
Stress friction adds the measured p99-minus-p90 visible-cost delta to actual boundary quotes; it is a sensitivity rather than historical private fill truth.
SP500 and SPCX are related equity-index markets and were screened as independent $500 reference accounts before any shared-capital portfolio construction.

The selected development result was already pooled-negative despite four positive folds, and both validation assets were negative; this supports rejection but does not establish that all order-book strategies fail on all HIP-3 markets.
No live profile, strategy, order, position, execution scope, backend process, or current portfolio configuration changed in this research revision.
